macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly pauses parts of its next model 'Astra' over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly suspended work on some aspects of its upcoming model Astra after internal concerns that it may have 'critical cyber capabilities.' The reported pause highlights how frontier model safety is increasingly shaping release timelines.

items.title: OpenAI brings unlimited text chats to free users
items.summary: OpenAI said ChatGPT free and Go users are now getting unlimited text chats, along with a new 'think' button for more complex queries. The update is part of a broader product push around ChatGPT access and usability.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents rather than human users. The release signals continued investment in agentic workflows and browser-based automation.

items.title: OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide
items.summary: OpenAI acquired NextSlide, a presentation startup whose team members are now working on ChatGPT. The deal adds to OpenAI's ongoing product and talent expansion efforts.

items.title: Apple reportedly plans to open its underlying AI technology to developers
items.summary: Reports say Apple is preparing to open its underlying AI technology to developers, which could broaden third-party integration across its ecosystem. The move would be a notable shift toward more developer-facing AI infrastructure.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Code for large code bases
items.summary: Meta reportedly launched Muse Code, an AI agent aimed at working across large code bases. The product reflects growing competition in developer tools and coding agents.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly in talks for a $10 billion cloud deal and exploring custom chips
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly pursuing a major cloud partnership and is also exploring its own custom AI chips, including talks with Samsung. The developments suggest the company is pushing harder on infrastructure control and compute strategy.

items.title: AI regulation and security discussions intensify in the U.S.
items.summary: U.S. officials and tech leaders are reportedly working on a voluntary security review process for advanced AI models before release, focused on closed models. The same theme is showing up in broader calls for AI safety testing and cybersecurity scrutiny.

items.title: AI virus-generation breakthrough raises biosecurity concerns
items.summary: Scientists reportedly used AI to create new kinds of viruses not found in nature, marking a major research milestone with significant safety implications. The result has sparked renewed discussion about how biological capabilities enabled by AI should be governed.

items.title: OpenAI, Google, and other frontier labs face growing pressure over model safety and release pace
items.summary: Recent coverage highlights a broader industry trend: frontier AI developers are being pushed to slow or modify releases when safety, cybersecurity, or misuse risks increase. This includes reporting on OpenAI's Astra work, shifting Google AI leadership, and intensified model-testing scrutiny.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA fully acquired by investor consortium and taken private
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Electronic Arts has been fully acquired by a trio of investor groups and is now a private company. This is the biggest industry-development item in the results and could affect EA’s future strategy and reporting structure.

items.title: Rockstar sets August 27 for an “extended look” at GTA 6
items.summary: Game Informer and PCMag both report that Rockstar has announced an “extended look” at Grand Theft Auto VI for August 27, with PCMag noting Netflix subscribers will get an early window before wider release. This is one of the most notable game-announcement items in the results.

items.title: Fortnite Festival Season 12 will headline Blackpink’s Lisa
items.summary: Rolling Stone reports that Lisa has been announced as the Season 12 headliner for Fortnite Festival, with the season set to debut later this month. This is a major live-service game and music-crossover announcement.

items.title: Nintendo says museum tickets must be bought only through official channels
items.summary: Nintendo Wire reports that Nintendo has warned fans to purchase Nintendo Museum tickets directly from the company and not through resale or third-party sellers. The warning follows reports of people being denied entry with improperly obtained tickets.

items.title: Nintendo digital sales surge and Switch 2 hardware tops 23 million
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Nintendo’s digital sales are up 90% compared with last year and that Switch 2 units have surpassed 23 million. The same report suggests continued strong momentum for Nintendo’s current hardware cycle.

items.title: Ghost Recon celebrates 25 years with Wildlands updates and new game confirmation
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Ubisoft released a 25th-anniversary Ghost Recon video, detailing free story and gameplay updates for Wildlands and confirming a new Ghost Recon game. This is a notable franchise update for tactical-shooter fans.

items.title: Helldivers 2 reveals new “Force of Law” Warbond
items.summary: GameRant reports that Helldivers 2 has revealed a new Force of Law Warbond for players. The announcement adds fresh post-launch content to Arrowhead’s co-op shooter.

items.title: Moonlighter 2 schedules 1.0 launch
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault will launch in 1.0 early next month, while the original Moonlighter is temporarily free. This is a notable release update for action-RPG fans.

items.title: Hackers reportedly seize Rainbow Six Siege backend and distribute billions in credits
items.summary: Gadgets Now reports that hackers took control of Rainbow Six Siege’s backend and distributed billions of in-game credits. If accurate, this is a major security and live-service integrity incident.

items.title: Xbox layoffs draw criticism from Doom developer
items.summary: GamesRadar reports that a Doom developer criticized Xbox after layoffs hit id Software, saying Microsoft ‘fundamentally don’t understand art’ and ‘don’t understand games.’ This is a notable industry reaction to the ongoing layoffs story.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Amazon data center plan raises major environmental concerns
items.summary: The New York Times reported that Amazon is planning a large Texas data center tied to an on-site natural-gas power plant that could become the most polluting in the U.S., highlighting a growing tension between cloud expansion and climate commitments.

items.title: Meta ordered to pay $567 million in New Mexico child safety case
items.summary: A state judge imposed a $567 million penalty on Meta, adding to a prior $375 million jury fine in a case alleging the company misled users about platform safety. The ruling is another major legal setback for the social media giant.

items.title: FCC removes long-standing cap on broadcast TV ownership
items.summary: The FCC lifted the rule that prevented a single television-station owner from reaching more than 39% of U.S. households. The move could reshape media ownership and consolidation in the broadcast industry.

items.title: TikTok lays off 250 employees in Nashville
items.summary: TikTok is cutting about 250 workers in its Nashville office, signaling continued restructuring inside the company. The move adds to broader uncertainty around the platform’s U.S. operations.

items.title: Unitree Robotics seeks about $900 million in IPO
items.summary: Unitree Robotics is reportedly aiming to raise roughly $900 million in an initial public offering, testing investor appetite for humanoid-robotics hardware. The listing would be a major milestone for the emerging robotics sector.

items.title: Google leadership shakeup follows departures of top researchers
items.summary: Google announced a leadership change in its AI organization shortly after four top researchers said they were leaving, underscoring continued churn at the company’s research ranks. The news points to internal reshuffling at a critical moment for Google’s product and research strategy.

items.title: X replaces revenue-sharing program with Original Content Rewards
items.summary: X is winding down its existing Revenue Sharing program and replacing it with a new Original Content Rewards system. The change reflects another shift in how the platform compensates creators.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf browser for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a browser designed for AI agents. The launch adds to the wave of infrastructure products aimed at automated web interaction.

items.title: Google warns of hackers targeting financial firms by phone
items.summary: Google’s security researchers said hackers are calling employees at large U.S. financial firms to break into systems and extort victims. The warning highlights a growing social-engineering threat to corporate cybersecurity.

items.title: Defense-tech startup Hadrian raises $1.37 billion
items.summary: Hadrian secured $1.37 billion at an $8 billion valuation, making it one of the largest recent defense-tech funding rounds. The deal signals strong investor interest in manufacturing and national-security technology.
